key_insight: An octopus‑inspired soft robotic arm embeds optoelectronic mechanosensors in its suction cups so peripheral (local) sensing and control can detect contact forces and infer object position, enabling reliable autonomous underwater grasping with reduced central computation.
problem_solved: Soft underwater manipulators lack distributed tactile feedback and low‑latency local control, making grasping in unstructured aquatic environments unreliable; this work provides a hardware+control solution for robust, decentralized grasping.
method: Design a compliant soft arm with suction cups that house optoelectronic mechanosensors to measure contact forces and local deformations.
Implement peripheral signal processing that converts sensor readings into contact location/force estimates and triggers local control actions, reducing reliance on central perception.
Validate via underwater experiments showing object localization and autonomous grasping, comparing success rates and latency to centralized approaches.
impact: Demonstrates a practical path for edge/embedded tactile sensing and decentralized control in robotic manipulation, informing ML/AI work on local inference, sensor fusion, and lightweight models for real‑time, resource‑constrained systems.

paper_title: Peripheral control enabled by distributed sensing in an octopus-inspired soft robotic arm for autonomous underwater grasping
paper_authors: Emanuela Del Dottore, Romina Adhami, Ebrahim Shahabi, Emanuele Solfiti, Michele Martini
